facts: From the native context, a node of a WebView's page with no checked state is no longer called not a checkbox: the refusal says it is part of a page and names switching to its context, where app_check now works.
A WebView page node that reads as disabled is refused saying a read-only field reads the same as a disabled one there, naming the WebView's context, never a wait.

Where the native tree reads the read-only field as enabled (Android 17), app_type and app_fill from the native context now go in through the page when it can be reached, so the field is refused with readonly attribute instead of taking the text.
note: 299 and 300 as drafted, both facts checked (internal/agent/check.go:63, handlers.go:1294 notEnabledInPage). ADD 301: the same read-only field on Android 17 read as enabled and took text from the native context — the second half of what changed for that field. The stored answer ('named by its label', 'readonly attribute') is the WebView-context behavior, not the native one; no doc problem behind it.
